incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: control-plane-deps-high-5xx (severity: P1). Observed spike in 5xx and timeouts across control plane calls to auth and org-lookup since ~4043210900 UTC

alice (oncall): seeing 502/504 trend in the dashboard, about ~30% of requests failing to downstream services. Impacting hosted API for some customers. Paging SRE.

bob (sre): on it. Can you confirm if this is global or region-specific? I see increased error budget burn across us-west and eu-west.

alice (oncall): hits in both regions. Top traces show failures at "controlplane.gateway" when calling auth-service and org-lookup with 5xx.

charlie (eng-runtime): adding context: we deployed a config roll two hours ago that adjusted heartbeat frequency for org-lookup caches. Could be related.

dana (product): any customer-facing impact? Support is getting a few reports of "service unavailable" in app flows.

eve (support): confirmed at least 3 tickets in last 10m for token validation failures; customers see 503 when calling /v1/generate.

bob (sre): initial mitigation checklist: 1) add temporary circuit-breaker for org-lookup on gateway, 2) increase retry/backoff in auth proxy, 3) roll back the config change if correlated. I'll open a runbook link: https://runbook/internal/cp-deps-5xx

alice (oncall): running quick query: auth lat p95 jumped from 45ms -> 1.2s, errors from 0.2% -> 28% over last 5m.

charlie (eng-runtime): can you dump the gateway logs where it calls org-lookup? I'll tail with filters.

bob (sre): running: kubectl -n controlplane logs -l app=gateway --since=10m | grep "org-lookup" > /tmp/gateway-orglog.txt. Early sign: upstream returned 502 with body 'timeout waiting for db'.

alice (oncall): @charlie do we have a fallback to cached org entries? If not, we should fail fast with cached IDs to preserve auth path.

charlie (eng-runtime): there is prefix KV cache but the config change reduced TTLs. I'm pushing a quick hotfix to increase TTL for org-lookup cache to 30s. Pushing now. Patch: 
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane-config/api/v1/update -d '{"org_lookup.ttl_secs":30}'
```

incident-bot: Deploy started by charlie (change-id: cfg-2026-1234). Estimated deploy time 45s.

bob (sre): while that deploy happens, enable a temporary rate-limit on gateway->org-lookup to reduce fanout. Setting to 200 rps per node.

alice (oncall): I see a drop in errors instantly after config change and rate-limit: error rate down to ~8% in 1m. latency p95 down to 350ms.

eve (support): confirming customers still seeing intermittent 503s but frequency reduced. Posting message to impacted customers: "We're aware of elevated 5xx; mitigation in progress; updates hourly."

charlie (eng-runtime): deploy is green. The TTL change is live on 90% of gateways (canary). Continuing rollout.

bob (sre): I want to triage root cause. Upstream logs show DB connection pool exhaustion at org-lookup backend after a heartbeat storm. Maybe the recent config adjusted heartbeats causing synchronized refreshes.

charlie (eng-runtime): yes that matches the earlier change. We reduced jitter in the refresh loop which inadvertently synchronized requests. Opening a rollback candidate: revert cfg-2026-1220 (heartbeat jitter).

alice (oncall): recommend we keep the TTL bump and rate-limit, and roll back heartbeat change. That keeps availability while avoiding DB overload.

dana (product): agree. Priority is minimizing customer-facing errors. Monitor for next 30m before full rollback if stable.

incident-bot: Change cfg-2026-1220 rollback scheduled by charlie. Initiating canary rollback to 10% of nodes.

bob (sre): also adding a temporary autoscaling rule for org-lookup deployment to spin extra pods (min replicas +3) to handle the load during the mitigation window. Applying now.

alice (oncall): applied. New replica count increased, pod restarts fine. Error rate down to ~1.5% now.

eve (support): updating customer comms: "Mitigation applied; most traffic restored. We'll continue monitoring and follow up with post-incident summary."

charlie (eng-runtime): can we capture a flamegraph / heap snapshot from org-lookup instances for postmortem? I'll request via the telemetry job.

bob (sre): doing a quick sweep of billing service traces — nothing correlated there, looks isolated to org-lookup + auth proxy fanout.

alice (oncall): good. I'm going to transition to handoff: paging window ends 30m from now. Bob to continue on-call for mitigation follow-up, charlie to own rollback and engineering root cause, dana to coordinate customer comms, eve to track tickets.

bob (sre): acknowledged. I'll keep the incident channel updated. Creating support ticket aggregation: INC-2026-0042.

charlie (eng-runtime): noted. I'll instrument the jitter in heartbeat and add a safety guard to avoid future syncs (randomized backoff).

dana (product): once stable, schedule a postmortem and impact assessment. Need list of affected customers and SLA exposures.

alice (oncall): last check: p50/p95 latencies back to normal, total 5xx rate ~0.7%. Closing pager.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident resolved by alice (oncall) at 4043211035. Follow-up: postmortem within 72h, assign charlie, bob, and dana.

bob (sre): quick notes for postmortem: root cause = heartbeat jitter removal -> synchronized org-lookup refresh -> DB pool exhaustion -> 502/504 at gateway. Mitigations = increased cache TTL, gateway rate-limit, autoscale, rollback heartbeat change.

charlie (eng-runtime): I'll draft the postmortem and include a timeline, recovery actions, and permanent fix plan (randomized jitter + safety circuit).

alice (oncall): thanks all. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
